candidate.answerReason: Two pairs of similar right triangles give AF=5BF/3 and CF=5BF/7. Adding these lengths gives AC=10, so BF=21/5.

methods.label: Express both parts of AC using BF
methods.explanation:
The right angles at \(A\) and \(C\) produce pairs of complementary angles, which let us compare the right triangles above and below \(AC\). Let \(h=BF\).

Because \(AB\perp AD\), \(\angle BAF\) complements \(\angle DAE\). In right triangle \(ADE\), \(\angle ADE\) also complements \(\angle DAE\). Thus \(\angle BAF=\angle ADE\). Together with the right angles at \(F\) and \(E\), this proves \(\triangle AFB\sim\triangle DEA\). Corresponding legs give
\[
\frac{AF}{DE}=\frac{BF}{EA},
\qquad AF=\frac{5h}{3}.
\]
Likewise, \(BC\perp CD\) gives
\[
\angle BCF=90^\circ-\angle DCE=\angle CDE.
\]
Therefore \(\triangle CFB\sim\triangle DEC\), so
\[
\frac{CF}{DE}=\frac{BF}{EC},
\qquad CF=\frac{5h}{7}.
\]
These two expressions help because \(AF\) and \(CF\) together make the known segment \(AC\). Since \(AC=AE+EC=3+7=10\),
\[
\frac{5h}{3}+\frac{5h}{7}=10.
\]
Multiplying by \(21\) yields \(35h+15h=210\), hence
\[
BF=h=\frac{21}{5}=4.2.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
